answer.label: Published by Clarke — credit traced through Lewis to Tolkien
answer.sourceLine: Clarke printed this concise joke while crediting C. S. Lewis, who had credited Tolkien with a similar conversational remark. Quote Investigator supports that chain rather than treating Clarke as the originator.

misattribution.heading: The wording and the thought
misattribution.intro: Clarke was transmitting a joke he credited to Lewis. Lewis’s own account traced a related question and answer to Tolkien; that oral history does not supply a verbatim Tolkien transcript.

items.why: Clarke credited Lewis rather than claiming independent origination; Lewis reported a related Tolkien remark. Read the transmission history ↗

misattribution.truthLine: Distinguish Clarke’s printed formulation from the earlier Lewis–Tolkien chain; no exact Tolkien transcript is established. Checked research ↗

sourcesVerified.claim: QI’s article transcribes Lewis’s 1966 collection and Clarke’s 1999 essay “Aspects of Science Fiction.” It explicitly treats the Tolkien evidence as indirect. The display spelling “Jailers” differs from the “Jailors” transcription in Clarke’s cited version.
